correctness.rationale: Proof gives unique affine extension for ranks at least two, exact binary-run transfer for nonzero translations, exact mirror-pair choices for nilpotent reflections, and exact correction for n(n−1) doubly counted nonzero rank-one maps. This establishes full joint rank/index polynomial for all n. Closed rank and total formulas follow by hockey-stick and parity counting; asymptotic density uses the credited known monoid order. Direct iteration over all partial injections n=1..8 and independent polynomial checks n=1..100 agree. Finite experiments are not the universal proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A distance-preserving partial map on a line has an affine extension in rank ≥2. Its nonzero translation restriction is nilpotent; its reflection restriction is nilpotent only when it avoids both fixed midpoints and complete mirror pairs. The prior rank and fixed-point enumerators aggregate over cyclic and acyclic maps, so they cannot by themselves yield the joint index and rank law. A matching equivalent theorem did not appear in actual searches; failure to find one is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Nilpotency index and rank jointly measure orbit lifetimes and support size of the natural finite inverse submonoid of chain isometries. The transfer gives all exact coefficients, the closed rank formula quantifies how many nilpotents occur at each natural height, the parity-resolved total proves a nonobvious asymptotic one-third density, and the extremal index multiplicities are sharp. Unlike unrefined known rank/fixedpoint counts, these distinguish fixedpoint-free involution restrictions from genuinely nilpotent maps. This is a motivated complete classification in an infinite family, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
